PMs are told to "define the problem"

yet, the rush to define the problem is where a lot of PMs go wrong.

before you define the problem, you have to observe, suspend judgement, resist even calling it a "problem"....just take it in.

Present instead...

"Wait, you all don't use user stories?"

"No. What for?"

"To have stories. How do you break stuff down?"

"The team meets, talks about it, maybe sketches, and then we build it"

"Without stories?"

"We might take notes. Or diagrams"

"And make them stories?"

"No. No stories"
Startups value ppl who can be flexible and fix the highest value challenges. Non-startups have trouble with this because it almost by definition challenges existing power structures.

I chat with lots of teams.

One thing is sadly clear.

That people let the dysfunction of their org seep into their self-identity, and talk themselves out of being able to get a better job.

And in some cases out of even considering the possibility.
without a strategy, all you are left with is a ton of good ideas, and no way to prioritize them
